thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate detected on inference-gateway (prod-us-east-1). Error rate > 8% over last 5m. Paging oncall-sre @mike. Rule: gateway_5xx_rate > 5%. 

mike (oncall-sre): saw it, joining. pulling logs now. 

mike (oncall-sre): quick summary from dashboards: 502/504 spike across front-door -> runtime-proxy. Token-level latency also increased. KV cache miss rate jumped from 2% -> 48% at ~2026-03-14T09:02Z. 

tess (eng-runtime): I see concurrent prefix-cache errors in runtime logs: 
```
2026-03-14T09:01:58Z runtime-proxy[pid=3421] ERROR kv_prefix_lookup: checksum mismatch for key=mdl:llm-v1:pref:abc123
2026-03-14T09:02:00Z runtime-proxy[pid=3421] WARN cache_eviction: reclaimed 12000 entries in 2s
2026-03-14T09:02:01Z runtime-proxy[pid=3421] ERROR runtime_request: upstream 502 gateway error, reason=kv_lookup_failure
```

liam (eng-platform): Hitting redis/kv cluster metrics — redis-a nodes show OOM evictions and forced eviction policy kicking in. Network IO looks ok. TTLs unchanged. Might be a cascading eviction (eviction cascade) when a new model version bloated prefix entries. 

mike (oncall-sre): can someone confirm recent deploys in prod? any model onboarding? 

tess (eng-runtime): There was a canary deploy 08:45Z that changed prefix key encoding for kv-layer (PR #1452). Canary was small but maybe an unexpected key size regression. I can revert canary if we think that's the cause. 

jana (support): CS flagged two enterprise tenants reporting 5xx failures in inference calls ~09:03Z. Tickets: INC-9482 and INC-9483. They are on Dedicated capacity but route through same routing plane. Notified customers that we are investigating. 

mike (oncall-sre): mitigation plan: 1) divert traffic to fallback routing (force route to last-known-good model variant) 2) scale up kv replica set + increase maxmemory to buy us time 3) if corruption confirmed, revert canary and restart runtime pods gracefully to force cache rebuild. Execute those in parallel. 

ops-bot: runbook: KV-CORRUPTION -> https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-corruption (page: eng-oncall) 

liam (eng-platform): scaling kv now: kubectl scale statefulset/kv-redis --replicas=5 -n infra; increasing maxmemory on redis-a to 24GB. Pushing config. ETA ~2m. 

mike (oncall-sre): enabling traffic fallback to variant v1-stable on gateway: 
```
POST /admin/route/override
{ "route": "inference", "variant": "v1-stable", "duration": 900 }
```
Response: 200 OK. 

tess (eng-runtime): starting graceful restart of runtime pods on nodepool rtm-*. Using rolling restart with 30s drain so KV prefix caches rebuild from persistent store. Command: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/runtime-proxy -n runtime --grace-period=30` 

mike (oncall-sre): observed customer error rate drop to ~3.8% after fallback + scale. Good. Keep monitoring. 

tess (eng-runtime): while restarting, I noticed some runtime instances complaining about corrupt RDB snapshot load: "ERR RDB CRC check failed" on redis-a-2 logs. That points to disk-level RDB corruption, not just eviction. 

liam (eng-platform): copying logs: 
```
Mar 14 09:03:12 redis-a-2 kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 4521 (redis-server)
Mar 14 09:03:13 redis-a-2 redis-server[4521]: # Fatal error, can't open the dump file: RDB CRC error
```

mike (oncall-sre): If RDB corrupted, best practice is to remove offending snapshot and let replicas sync from master. We'll take redis-a-2 out of rotation. liam, can you fence it? 

liam (eng-platform): done: marked redis-a-2 read-only and removed from SRV set. Initiating replica resync from healthy master. Also uploading previous clean snapshot to S3 as fallback. 

jana (support): customer update: notified affected tenants that we mitigated the 5xx by routing to stable variant and scaling kv. Provided ETA for full resolution: 2-4 hours. Team requests follow-up postmortem and customer impact numbers. 

mike (oncall-sre): next: run a KV consistency check across nodes and confirm no keyspace corruption remains. tess, can runtime tolerate cache rebuild? We might see a small latency bump. 

tess (eng-runtime): runtime can handle rebuilds; we have prefix caching warmers but expect 10-20% latency increase for ~15 minutes for cold prefixes. Proceeding with full cache invalidation on nodes with corrupted reads: `curl -XPOST http://runtime-proxy/admin/cache/invalidate?prefix=mdl:llm-v1` and restarting. 

incident-bot: Handoff scheduled: mike -> tess at 09:40Z for mitigation ops, mike remains as incident commander for coordination and customer comms. 

mike (oncall-sre): handoff noted, tess please run deeper investigation: - full list of keys with checksum failures - compare RDB snapshots - list of pods that loaded corrupt snapshot 

tess (eng-runtime): started a script to scan recent logs and collect candidate keys: `python tools/scan_kv_logs.py --since 09:00 --pattern checksum` will upload results to /tmp/kv-checks-1779004321.json (artifact saved to S3) 

liam (eng-platform): replica resync completed on redis-a-2, no RDB CRC on new load. maxmemory increased cluster-wide. Eviction policy changed to volatile-lru for protected prefixes. 

mike (oncall-sre): metrics update: total 5xx dropped to 1.2% over last 5m. Customer-visible errors for affected tenants reduced to negligible. 

jana (support): CS will close high-priority alerts for the two tenants once we confirm stable for 30m. 

ops-bot: ACTION LOG: scaled kv replicas; removed corrupted node; restarted runtime-proxy; enabled routing fallback; invalidated corrupted prefixes; oncall handoff complete. 

mike (oncall-sre): we'll keep this incident open for full post-incident analysis. Please add notes to INC-2026-03-14-01. Owners: postmortem=tess, remediation=liam, customer-comm=jana. 

tess (eng-runtime): adding immediate action items: 1) revert PR #1452 key-encoding change in prod and add stricter key-size unit tests; 2) add RDB integrity checks in redis startup alerting; 3) add smoother fallback that avoids full cache invalidation. 

liam (eng-platform): follow-ups: automated snapshot uploads every 10m to warm S3-backed restores, increase maxmemory by 25% for peak windows, and a canary gating flag for key-format changes. 

mike (oncall-sre): final note: customer impact classification: Sev2 (partial service degradation for a subset of customers), duration ~45 minutes peak, mitigated by routing fallback and kv scale + node fencing. Will await postmortem. :white_check_mark: 

jana (support): noted. closing channel for live mitigation. We'll reopen if any regressions. Thanks team :heart:
